Bail Bond Information for Bexar County

After booking into Bexar County jail, a judge typically sets bail at arraignment (often within 24–72 hours). Families often work with a licensed bail bondsman. A common commercial bond fee is about 10% of the bail amount (non-refundable). Example: $10,000 bail → roughly $1,000 premium, subject to local rules.

If the person cannot afford bail, they may request a reduction hearing or public defender.

For hearing schedules, contact the Bexar County court.

Visitation Rules at Bexar County Jail

Policies vary. Before visiting Bexar County Adult Detention Center, confirm:

  • Approved ID: Government-issued photo ID
  • Hours: Call Bexar County Sheriff's Office for the current schedule
  • Dress code: Facilities restrict clothing that resembles uniforms
  • Video visits: Many jails offer remote options — ask when you call
  • Children: Minors usually need an accompanying adult

What to Expect After Arrest in Bexar County

Typical steps after arrest in Bexar County:

  1. Booking — fingerprints, photo, property inventory
  2. Medical screening — before general population housing
  3. Classification — housing based on charges and history
  4. Arraignment — first court appearance; bail often set here
  5. Transfer — serious cases may move to a state facility

Frequently Asked Questions — Bexar County Inmate Lookup

How do I find out if someone is in Bexar County jail?

Use the official Bexar County inmate roster or call the jail directly. You can also call (210) 335-6201 to speak with staff. Records often lag 2–8 hours after booking.

How long does booking take in Bexar County?

Booking often takes 2–8 hours depending on volume. Weekends and holidays can delay when a name appears in any published system.

Can I visit an inmate at Bexar County jail?

Usually yes if the facility allows visits and the person is eligible. The main facility is located at 200 N Comal St, San Antonio, TX 78207. Contact Bexar County Adult Detention Center for hours, ID rules, and dress code. Video visitation may be available.

What if the person is not in the county jail system?

They may be in state custody — check the Texas DOC. For federal charges use the BOP inmate locator.

How do I send money to an inmate in Bexar County?

Most facilities use a commissary vendor (for example JPay, Securus, or Access Corrections). Confirm the vendor and limits with Bexar County Adult Detention Center before sending funds.
